Mesh lets nearby phones connect directly to each other, without the internet or a cell signal.\n\nEach phone in the mesh can send, receive, and pass along data for the others.
As many as you want! Every device serves a purpose, so if you aren\'t using it to send or receive data, your device will act as a middleman so no node is wasted!
Why is it better than Wi-Fi? And when is it best applied?

Regular Wi-Fi depends on a single router. If you move too far from it, or it stops working, you lose the connection.

• Mesh has no central router. Phones connect to each other directly.
• If one device leaves, the others can stay connected.

Summary: Wi-Fi works best at home or in the office. Mesh is useful where there is no router or internet.
• One phone opens the Home tab and taps Start Hotspot.\n• Other phones join by scanning that phone\'s QR code, or by opening a connect link shared with them.
To disconnect, turn off Mesh in the app. The rest of the network keeps working without you.

Mesh exercises end-to-end encryption via keys. This is utilized on all internet traffic, meaning outsiders cannot see what you are browsing or the messages you are sending or receiving. Essentially, it is as safe as any safe system out there.\n\nThe only exception may be that your device will have a node number that will be visible to other nodes in the system, and if you utilize any location applications like GPS, either your coordinates or your node number will be shared with other nodes.

For the device hosting the hotspot, you can choose between 2.4GHz and 5GHz:
• 2.4GHz: Longer distances and deeper penetration of obstacles (walls and furniture).
• 5GHz: Faster speeds with less range and penetration.

Otherwise, this depends on whether you are referring to your phone or between nodes:
• A phone's range is dependent on the device's Bluetooth distance frequency. However, average max distances on Bluetooth connections can vary between 50 and 150 feet. This is the distance between your phone and a node in the Mesh network.
• Between node to node: This is limited to the amount of physical hardware available: antennas, electrical power, obstacles. The frequency band you use, 2.4–5GHz or sub-GHz, will determine if the range is similar to that of Bluetooth or miles in distance.

• If you have a non-mobile node, then your battery life is dependent on you charging your device, whether it be in a public, private, residential or commercial location.\n• For a mobile device, like your phone, as long as you remain connected to the Mesh network, your device is actively participating in the entire system. This means that if you aren\'t sending or receiving, your device can act as a \'middleman\', moving data packets along a predetermined path. This can and will exhaust battery life. The best solution would be to disconnect and reconnect only when you need to.

Mesh is most useful where the internet or cell service is unavailable or unreliable.

• Disasters: Mesh does not depend on city infrastructure, so rescuers and first responders can keep communicating. If a user is out of range, messages can be passed along through other devices.
• Outages and remote areas: Mesh keeps nearby people connected during power or network outages, or where there is no signal.

• Home: The home page is where you set up and initiate your Mesh network OR join another via Wi-Fi Connect, URI link, or QR code.
• Network: This page is where you can view your or other networks in the area. The network name is displayed, along with connection stability, status (on/off), and the number of nodes or 'hops' in the network. This means the number of devices your data will traverse to reach its destination.
• Send: This page is dedicated to sending data, whether it be files, photos, videos, or anything in between. You simply select the file, choose the recipient, then send. It creates a list of data sent, so you can keep track of what you've sent, when, and to whom.
• Receive: This page is all about what gets sent to YOU! It creates a list based on the date and order received. You can choose to either download them to your gallery, send them elsewhere, or save to a specific folder.
• Chat: This is the place where you have one-on-one conversations with other nodes in the network (other devices that can receive and respond). You have a prelude screen, where you can see multiple conversations, their status and stability, and a preview of the most recent message. When you click a specific device, you enter the chatroom where you can type and read your chats.
• Log: A technical record of app activity, used for troubleshooting.
• Settings: The place where you can customize the entire application, see where the Project Mesh folder is located, and change the device's name if you so choose.
Can I still use Bluetooth for my headphones?
Can I log back into my chat via another phone?
Sadly no. Your chats can be saved, but they are saved onto the device used. Each node is unique.
Any Android device running Android 10 or later can use Project Mesh, while any nodes capable of acting as a middleman can operate within the Mesh network.

Meshrabiya is the open-source peer-to-peer networking library behind Wi-Fi Direct and virtual network routing in Project Mesh. It sets up direct local Wi-Fi connections, gives each device a virtual IP address, and forms multi-hop mesh paths without an internet connection or router.
Project Mesh uses meshrabiya:// as its custom URI scheme.

When a device creates a connect link or QR code, it starts the link with meshrabiya:// so Project Mesh can read the Wi-Fi details (network name, password, port and virtual address) needed to join that device\'s hotspot.
URI stands for Uniform Resource Identifier: a standard string that identifies a resource, such as a webpage, file or network endpoint, so apps can find and use it.

Can I use the URI connect method with Wi-Fi Direct?
No. The URI method only works with Local.

Quick Share says "Can't share 1 file because Wi-Fi Direct is already in use on your phone." What should I do?
Restart your device or the other device. One of them is still using Wi-Fi Direct.

Which band should I use?
5 GHz is faster. 2.4 GHz reaches farther and passes through walls and furniture better, but is slower.

Can I change the hotspot type without losing my connection?
No. You will be disconnected and need to reconnect with the QR code or URI.

What happens if I use Local while connected to a Wi-Fi router?
Your device leaves the router and switches to hotspot mode, ready for other devices to connect.

Can I still use Quick Share with Wi-Fi Direct or Local?
Yes. Use Quick Share to send the connect URI to the other device.
The Log page shows the live diagnostic log from Meshrabiya, where real-time network events are recorded. It is mainly useful for Project Mesh developers. Here is how to read one line:
[15:16:52.29]: the time of the event (hours, minutes, seconds, hundredths).
WifiDirectManager: the part of the networking engine that handled the event.
169.254.33.215: the virtual mesh address of the device that logged it.
Wifi2pChannel initialized: what happened. Here, the Wi-Fi Direct (P2P) channel opened successfully.
